passages.title: 丑马牛仔的难忘一跑
passages.genre: 记叙文 · 人与动物
passages.summary: 十三岁那年，“我”经历了父母离婚、重组家庭和搬家，心爱的小马也被卖掉，整日伤心哭泣。父亲给“我”买了一匹又老又丑的红马牛仔，“我”在马术俱乐部里受尽嘲笑，绕桶赛中又输给了贝基，于是每天苦练，可到了比赛那天仍没有信心。续写两段的开头语分别是“终于轮到我了”和“我跑完时，场上没有一声欢呼”。

paras.en: A Run to Remember
paras.zh: 难忘的一跑

paras.en: Thirteen can be a challenging age.
paras.zh: 十三岁可能是个充满挑战的年纪。

w.m: adj. 有挑战性的；艰难的

paras.en: Not only did I have to adapt to my changing body, but I also had to deal with my parents’ bitter divorce, a new family and the upsetting move from my country home to a crowded suburb.
paras.zh: 我不仅得适应自己正在变化的身体，还得面对父母充满怨恨的离婚、一个新的家庭，以及从乡下的家搬到拥挤的郊区这桩让人难过的事。

w.m: 不仅……而且（not only 置于句首倒装）
adj. 充满怨恨的；激烈的

paras.en: When we moved, my beloved companion, a small brown pony (小马), had to be sold.
paras.zh: 搬家时，我心爱的伙伴——一匹棕色的小马——不得不卖掉了。

paras.en: Feeling helpless and alone, I couldn’t eat or sleep, and I cried all of the time.
paras.zh: 我觉得无助又孤单，吃不下也睡不着，整天哭个不停。

paras.en: I missed my family, my home and my pony.
paras.zh: 我想念我的家人、我的家，还有我的小马。

paras.en: Finally, my father, realizing how much I missed my pony, purchased an old red horse for me at a local market.
paras.zh: 最后，父亲意识到我有多想念那匹小马，就在当地的集市上给我买了一匹老红马。

paras.en: My horse, Cowboy, was without a doubt the ugliest horse in the world.
paras.zh: 我的马叫牛仔，毫无疑问，它是世界上最丑的马。

paras.en: He was pigeon-toed and knock-kneed.
paras.zh: 它脚尖内八，膝盖外翻。

paras.en: But I didn’t care about his faults.
paras.zh: 可我并不在乎它的这些缺点。

paras.en: I loved him beyond all reason.
paras.zh: 我爱它，爱得不讲任何道理。

w.m: 毫无道理地；不可理喻地

paras.en: I joined a riding club and faced rude comments and mean snickers about Cowboy’s looks.
paras.zh: 我加入了一个马术俱乐部，却要面对别人对牛仔长相的冷言冷语和刻薄窃笑。

paras.en: I never let on how I felt, but deep down inside, my heart was breaking.
paras.zh: 我从没流露过自己的感受，可在内心深处，我的心都要碎了。

paras.en: The other members rode beautiful registered horses.
paras.zh: 其他成员骑的都是漂亮的登记在册的纯种马。

w.m: adj. 登记注册的（指有血统登记的纯种马）

paras.en: When Cowboy and I entered the events where the horse is judged on appearance, we were quickly out of the game.
paras.zh: 牛仔和我参加按马匹外形评分的比赛项目时，很快就被淘汰了。

paras.en: I finally realized that my only chance to compete would be in the timed-speed events.
paras.zh: 我终于意识到，我唯一能参赛的机会就是计时竞速项目。

paras.en: I chose barrel racing (绕桶赛), an event in which a horse and its rider attempt to complete a triangular pattern around three barrels in the fastest time.
paras.zh: 我选了绕桶赛，在这个项目里，马和骑手要用最快的时间绕三个桶跑完一个三角形路线。

paras.en: One girl named Becky rode a big brown horse in the race events.
paras.zh: 有个叫贝基的女孩，在竞速项目中骑一匹高大的棕马。

paras.en: She always won the blue ribbons.
paras.zh: 她总是拿蓝绶带。

paras.en: Needless to say, she didn’t feel threatened when I competed against her at the next show.
paras.zh: 不用说，下一场比赛我和她同场较量时，她根本没觉得受到威胁。

paras.en: She didn’t need to.
paras.zh: 她也确实没必要。

paras.en: I came in next to last.
paras.zh: 我得了倒数第二。

paras.en: The bitter memory of Becky’s smirks (得意的笑) made me determined to beat her.
paras.zh: 一想起贝基那得意的笑，我就心里发苦，下定决心要打败她。

paras.en: For the whole next month, I woke up early every day and rode Cowboy five miles to the arena (运动场地).
paras.zh: 接下来的一整个月，我每天都早早起床，骑着牛仔跑五英里去运动场。

paras.en: We practiced for hours in the hot sun and then I would walk Cowboy home.
paras.zh: 我们顶着烈日一练就是几个小时，然后我总是牵着牛仔走回家。

paras.en: On the way home I would be so tired; those five miles seemed twice as long.
paras.zh: 回家的路上我总是累得要命，那五英里似乎有平时的两倍长。

paras.en: All of our hard work didn’t make me feel confident by the time the show came.
paras.zh: 尽管我们这么刻苦地练习，到比赛来临时，我还是没有信心。

paras.en: I sat at the gate and sweated it out while I watched Becky and her horse charge through the pattern of barrels, finishing the course with ease.
paras.zh: 我坐在门口，忐忑地熬着，看着贝基和她的马冲过一个个桶，轻轻松松跑完了全程。

paras.en: My turn finally came.
paras.zh: 终于轮到我了。

paras.en: No cheers filled the air when I finished my show.
paras.zh: 我跑完时，场上没有一声欢呼。

passages.title: 路边相助的墨西哥一家
passages.genre: 记叙文 · 善意与互助
passages.summary: 过去一年，“我”的车出了三次故障，大多数人都懒得帮忙，让“我”很是厌烦。有一次，“我”在路边等了近三个小时，一个墨西哥家庭停车相助：父亲借来千斤顶、锯木头垫底，母亲开车去买新的轮胎扳手，帮“我”换好了轮子，却不肯收“我”的钱。续写两段的开头语分别是“我正要道别时，小女孩问我吃过午饭没有”和“他们走后，我坐进吉普车，打开了那个纸袋”。

paras.en: During this past year, I’ve had three instances of car trouble.
paras.zh: 过去这一年里，我的车出过三次毛病。

paras.en: Each time these things happened, I was sick of the way most people hadn’t bothered to help.
paras.zh: 每次出这种事，大多数人都懒得帮忙，这让我很是厌烦。

paras.en: One of those times, I was on the side of the road for close to three hours with my big Jeep.
paras.zh: 其中有一次，我开着那辆大吉普车，在路边困了将近三个小时。

w.h: on the side of the road

paras.en: I put signs in the windows, big signs that said NEED A JACK (千斤顶), and offered money.
paras.zh: 我在车窗上贴了牌子，大大的牌子上写着“需要千斤顶”，还说愿意出钱。

paras.en: Nothing.
paras.zh: 毫无回应。

w.m: pron. 什么都没有（此处指毫无回应）

paras.en: Right as I was about to give up, a Mexican family in a small truck pulled over, and the father bounded out.
paras.zh: 就在我快要放弃的时候，一个墨西哥家庭开着一辆小卡车靠边停下，那位父亲一跃跳下车来。

paras.en: He sized up the situation and called for his daughter, who spoke English.
paras.zh: 他打量了一下情况，把会说英语的女儿叫了过来。

paras.en: He conveyed through her that he had a jack but that it was too small for the Jeep, so we would need something to support it.
paras.zh: 他通过女儿告诉我，他有一个千斤顶，可对吉普车来说太小了，所以我们得找个东西把它垫高。

paras.en: Then he got a saw (锯子) from the truck and cut a section out of a big log on the side of the road.
paras.zh: 接着，他从卡车上拿了一把锯子，从路边一根大圆木上锯下一截。

paras.en: We rolled it over and put his jack on top, and we were in business.
paras.zh: 我们把木头滚过来，把他的千斤顶放在上面，这下就能干活了。

paras.en: I started taking the wheel off, and then, if you can believe it, I broke his tire iron.
paras.zh: 我开始拆轮子，接着，说出来你都不信，我把他的轮胎扳手弄断了。

paras.en: No worries: He handed it to his wife, and she was gone in a flash down the road to buy a new tire iron.
paras.zh: 没关系：他把扳手递给妻子，她一眨眼就沿着路开走了，去买一把新的轮胎扳手。

paras.en: She was back in 15 minutes.
paras.zh: 十五分钟后她就回来了。

paras.en: We finished the job, and I was a very happy man.
paras.zh: 我们干完了活，我开心极了。

paras.en: The two of us were dirty and sweaty.
paras.zh: 我们俩又脏又满身是汗。

w.m: adj. 汗流浃背的；满是汗的

paras.en: His wife prepared a pot of water for us to wash our hands.
paras.zh: 他妻子准备了一盆水，让我们洗手。

paras.en: I tried to put a $20 bill in the man’s hand, but he wouldn’t take it, so instead I went up to the truck and gave it to his wife as quietly as I could.
paras.zh: 我想把一张二十美元的钞票塞到那人手里，可他不肯收，于是我转而走到卡车那边，尽量不声不响地把钱给了他妻子。

paras.en: I asked the little girl where they lived.
paras.zh: 我问小女孩他们住在哪儿。

paras.en: Mexico, she said.
paras.zh: 墨西哥，她说。

paras.en: They were in Oregon so Mommy and Daddy could work on a fruit farm for the next few weeks.
paras.zh: 他们来俄勒冈，是为了让爸爸妈妈接下来几个星期在一家水果农场干活。

paras.en: Then they would go home.
paras.zh: 然后他们就要回家了。

paras.en: When I was about to say goodbye, the girl asked if I’d had lunch.
paras.zh: 我正要道别时，小女孩问我吃过午饭没有。

paras.en: After they left, I got into my Jeep and opened the paper bag.
paras.zh: 他们走后，我坐进吉普车，打开了那个纸袋。

passages.title: 营地外的北极熊
passages.genre: 记叙文 · 人与自然
passages.summary: 一年秋天，“我”和妻子埃莉住在加拿大丘吉尔镇外的研究营地拍北极熊。一头年轻的雄性北极熊闻到大蒜面包的香味，跑来撕扯营地的铁丝围栏，喊叫、敲锅、空包弹都吓不走它；营地负责人说直升机半小时后才到，建议用胡椒喷雾，熊被喷后跑去湖边洗眼睛。续写两段的开头语分别是“几分钟后，那头熊又朝我们的营地走了回来”和“就在那一刻，直升机到了”。

paras.en: One fall, my wife Elli and I had a single goal: to photograph polar bears.
paras.zh: 一年秋天，我和妻子埃莉只有一个目标：拍北极熊。

paras.en: We were staying at a research camp outside “the polar bear capital of the world”—the town of Churchill in Manitoba, Canada.
paras.zh: 我们住在“世界北极熊之都”——加拿大马尼托巴省的丘吉尔镇——外面的一个研究营地里。

paras.en: Taking pictures of polar bears is amazing but also dangerous.
paras.zh: 拍北极熊很精彩，却也很危险。

paras.en: Polar bears—like all wild animals—should be photographed from a safe distance.
paras.zh: 北极熊和所有野生动物一样，应该在安全距离之外拍摄。

paras.en: When I’m face to face with a polar bear, I like it to be through a camera with a telephoto lens.
paras.zh: 和北极熊面对面时，我希望中间隔着一台装了长焦镜头的相机。

paras.en: But sometimes, that is easier said than done.
paras.zh: 可有时候，说起来容易做起来难。

paras.en: This was one of those times.
paras.zh: 这次就是其中之一。

paras.en: As Elli and I cooked dinner, a young male polar bear who was playing in a nearby lake sniffed, and smelled our garlic bread.
paras.zh: 我和埃莉做晚饭时，一头在附近湖里玩耍的年轻雄性北极熊嗅了嗅，闻到了我们的大蒜面包。

paras.en: The hungry bear followed his nose to our camp, which was surrounded by a high wire fence.
paras.zh: 饥饿的熊循着气味来到了我们的营地，营地四周围着高高的铁丝网。

paras.en: He pulled and bit the wire.
paras.zh: 它又扯又咬铁丝网。

paras.en: He stood on his back legs and pushed at the wooden fence posts.
paras.zh: 它用后腿站立，推着围栏的木桩。

paras.en: Terrified, Elli and I tried all the bear defense actions we knew.
paras.zh: 我和埃莉吓坏了，把知道的防熊招数全都试了一遍。

paras.en: We yelled at the bear, hit pots hard, and fired blank shotgun shells into the air.
paras.zh: 我们冲着熊大喊，使劲敲锅，还朝天空发射霰弹枪的空包弹。

paras.en: Sometimes loud noises like these will scare bears off.
paras.zh: 有时候，这样的巨响会把熊吓跑。

paras.en: Not this polar bear though—he just kept trying to tear down the fence with his massive paws (爪子).
paras.zh: 可这头北极熊不吃这一套——它只是用巨大的爪子不停地想把围栏扯倒。

paras.en: I radioed the camp manager for help.
paras.zh: 我用无线电向营地负责人求救。

paras.en: He told me a helicopter was on its way, but it would be 30 minutes before it arrived.
paras.zh: 他告诉我，直升机已经在路上了，不过还要三十分钟才能到。

paras.en: Making the best of this close encounter (相遇), I took some pictures of the bear.
paras.zh: 趁着这次近距离相遇，我给熊拍了几张照片。

paras.en: Elli and I feared the fence wouldn’t last through 30 more minutes of the bear’s punishment.
paras.zh: 我和埃莉担心，围栏再经受这头熊三十分钟的折腾，就撑不住了。

paras.en: The camp manager suggested I use pepper spray.
paras.zh: 营地负责人建议我用胡椒喷雾。

paras.en: The spray burns the bears’ eyes, but doesn’t hurt them.
paras.zh: 这种喷雾会让熊的眼睛火辣辣地疼，但不会伤到它们。

paras.en: So I approached our uninvited guest slowly and, through the fence, sprayed him in the face.
paras.zh: 于是我慢慢走近这位不速之客，隔着围栏朝它脸上喷了一下。

paras.en: With an angry roar (吼叫), the bear ran to the lake to wash his eyes.
paras.zh: 熊愤怒地吼叫一声，跑到湖边去洗眼睛。

paras.en: A few minutes later, the bear headed back to our camp.
paras.zh: 几分钟后，那头熊又朝我们的营地走了回来。

paras.en: At that very moment, the helicopter arrived.
paras.zh: 就在那一刻，直升机到了。

passages.title: 帮伯纳德卖爆米花
passages.genre: 记叙文 · 善意与互助
passages.summary: 经济不景气，小镇上不少家庭难以维持生计。热心的梅雷迪思太太常去探望穷人，她向孩子们说起一户困难人家的小男孩伯纳德：他很想挣钱，却不知道能做什么；大儿子约翰想出主意，用约翰叔叔寄来的玉米做爆米花，让伯纳德挨家挨户去卖。续写两段的开头语分别是“梅雷迪思太太听说了约翰的主意，也觉得很好”和“一切准备就绪，伯纳德开始了他的新生意”。

paras.en: The Meredith family lived in a small community.
paras.zh: 梅雷迪思一家住在一个小社区里。

paras.en: As the economy was in decline, some people in the town had lost their jobs.
paras.zh: 由于经济衰退，镇上有些人丢了工作。

paras.en: Many of their families were struggling to make ends meet.
paras.zh: 他们中很多人的家里都在艰难度日，勉强维持生计。

paras.en: People were trying to help each other meet the challenges.
paras.zh: 人们都在设法互相帮助，共渡难关。

paras.en: Mrs. Meredith was a most kind and thoughtful woman.
paras.zh: 梅雷迪思太太是一位非常善良、体贴的女士。

w.m: 非常善良的（most 表示“非常”）
adj. 体贴的；关心他人的

paras.en: She spent a great deal of time visiting the poor.
paras.zh: 她花了大量时间去探望穷人。

paras.en: She knew they had problems, and they needed all kinds of help.
paras.zh: 她知道他们有困难，需要各种各样的帮助。

paras.en: When she had time, she would bring food and medicine to them.
paras.zh: 她一有空，就会给他们送去食物和药品。

paras.en: One morning she told her children about a family she had visited the day before.
paras.zh: 一天早上，她跟孩子们讲起了她前一天探望过的一户人家。

paras.en: There was a man sick in bed, his wife, who took care of him and could not go out to work, and their little boy.
paras.zh: 这家有一个卧病在床的男人，他的妻子要照顾他，没法出去工作，还有他们的小儿子。

paras.en: The little boy—his name was Bernard—had interested her very much.
paras.zh: 那个小男孩名叫伯纳德，让她很感兴趣。

paras.en: “I wish you could see him,” she said to her own children, John, Harry, and Clara.
paras.zh: “真希望你们能见见他。”她对自己的孩子约翰、哈里和克拉拉说。

w.m: 真希望你们能（虚拟语气）

paras.en: “He is such a help to his mother.
paras.zh: “他可真是妈妈的好帮手。

paras.en: He wants very much to earn some money, but I don’t see what he can do.”
paras.zh: 他非常想挣点钱，可我看不出他能做什么。”

paras.en: After their mother left the room, the children sat thinking about Bernard.
paras.zh: 妈妈离开房间后，孩子们坐在那里想着伯纳德的事。

w.m: 坐着想（分词作伴随状语）

paras.en: “I wish we could help him to earn money,” said Clara.
paras.zh: “真希望我们能帮他挣到钱。”克拉拉说。

w.m: 真希望我们能（虚拟语气）

paras.en: “His family is suffering so much.”
paras.zh: “他家日子太苦了。”

paras.en: “So do I,” said Harry.
paras.zh: “我也这么想。”哈里说。

w.m: 我也是（so 置于句首倒装）

paras.en: “We really should do something to assist them.”
paras.zh: “我们真该做点什么来帮帮他们。”

paras.en: For some moments, John said nothing, but, suddenly, he sprang to his feet and cried, “I have a great idea!
paras.zh: 约翰好一会儿都没说话，可突然，他一下子跳起来，喊道：“我有个好主意！

paras.en: I have a solution that we can all help accomplish (完成).”
paras.zh: 我有个办法，咱们都能出份力，帮着把这事办成。”

paras.en: The other children also jumped up, all attention.
paras.zh: 其他孩子也跳了起来，全神贯注地听着。

paras.en: When John had an idea, it was sure to be a good one.
paras.zh: 约翰一有主意，那准是个好主意。

paras.en: “I tell you what we can do,” said John.
paras.zh: “我来告诉你们咱们能做什么。”约翰说。

w.m: 我来告诉你们（引出建议）

paras.en: “You know that big box of corn Uncle John sent us?
paras.zh: “还记得约翰叔叔寄给我们的那一大箱玉米吗？

paras.en: Well, we can make popcorn (爆米花), and put it into paper bags, and Bernard can take it around to the houses and sell it.”
paras.zh: 嗯，我们可以做爆米花，装进纸袋，让伯纳德挨家挨户去卖。”

paras.en: When Mrs. Meredith heard of John’s idea, she thought it was a good one, too.
paras.zh: 梅雷迪思太太听说了约翰的主意，也觉得很好。

paras.en: With everything ready, Bernard started out on his new business.
paras.zh: 一切准备就绪，伯纳德开始了他的新生意。

w.m: 一切准备就绪（with复合结构）

passages.title: 老狗波比的新伙伴
passages.genre: 记叙文 · 人与动物
passages.summary: 男孩离家去上大学，父母开车送他，与他含泪道别，老狗波比也跟着回了家。男孩走后，家里冷冷清清，波比整整一周对吃饭、玩具、散步都提不起兴趣，主人想尽办法也没能让它高兴起来；妈妈提议给波比找只小狗作伴，不久两人抱回一个大箱子，波比闻到气味后，尾巴慢慢摇了起来。续写两段的开头语分别是“爸爸打开箱子，一只可爱的小狗出现了”和“几个星期后，男孩从大学回到了家”。

paras.en: “I’m going to miss you so much, Poppy,” said the tall, thin teenager.
paras.zh: “我会非常想你的，波比。”这个又高又瘦的少年说。

paras.en: He bent down to hug his old friend goodbye.
paras.zh: 他弯下腰，抱了抱他的老朋友，跟它道别。

paras.en: He stood up, hugged his parents, and smiled, trying not to let his emotions (情绪) get the better of him.
paras.zh: 他站起身，拥抱了父母，笑了笑，努力不让情绪失控。

paras.en: His parents were not quite able to keep theirs under control.
paras.zh: 他的父母却没能完全控制住自己的情绪。

paras.en: They had driven their son several hours out of town to the university where he would soon be living and studying.
paras.zh: 他们开了几个小时的车，把儿子送到城外的大学，不久他就要在那里生活和学习了。

paras.en: It was time to say goodbye for now at least.
paras.zh: 是时候说再见了，至少暂时如此。

paras.en: The family hugged and smiled through misty eyes and then laughed.
paras.zh: 一家人拥抱在一起，含着泪微笑，接着又笑出了声。

paras.en: The boy lifted the last bag onto his shoulder, and flashed a bright smile.
paras.zh: 男孩把最后一个包扛上肩膀，露出灿烂的笑容。

paras.en: “I guess this is it,” he said.
paras.zh: “我想就到这儿了。”他说。

w.m: 就到这儿了；就是这一刻了

paras.en: “I’ll see you back home in a month, okay?”
paras.zh: “一个月后家里见，好吗？”

paras.en: His parents nodded, and they watched as he walked out of sight into the crowds of hundreds of students and parents.
paras.zh: 父母点了点头，看着他走进成百上千的学生和家长人群中，直到看不见他的身影。

paras.en: The boy’s mother turned to the dog and said, “Okay, Poppy, time to go back home.”
paras.zh: 男孩的妈妈转向小狗说：“好了，波比，该回家了。”

paras.en: The house seemed quiet as a tomb without the boy living there.
paras.zh: 男孩不在家住了，屋里安静得像坟墓一样。

w.m: 像坟墓一样安静；死一般寂静（tomb：坟墓）

paras.en: All that week, Poppy didn’t seem interested in her dinner, her favorite toy, or even in her daily walk.
paras.zh: 那一整周，波比对晚饭、最喜欢的玩具，甚至每天的散步，似乎都提不起兴趣。

paras.en: Her owners were sad too, but they knew their son would be back to visit.
paras.zh: 它的主人也很难过，可他们知道儿子会回来看看的。

paras.en: Poppy didn’t.
paras.zh: 波比却不知道。

paras.en: They offered the dog some of her favorite peanut butter treats.
paras.zh: 他们给小狗喂它最爱吃的花生酱零食。

paras.en: They even let her sit on the sofa, but the old girl just wasn’t her usual cheerful self.
paras.zh: 他们甚至让它坐到沙发上，可这只老狗就是没有平时那样快活。

paras.en: Her owners started to get worried.
paras.zh: 主人开始担心起来。

paras.en: “What should we do to cheer Poppy up?” asked Dad.
paras.zh: “我们该怎么做才能让波比高兴起来呢？”爸爸问。

paras.en: “We’ve tried everything.”
paras.zh: “能试的我们都试过了。”

paras.en: “I have an idea, but it might be a little crazy,” smiled Mom.
paras.zh: “我有个主意，不过可能有点疯狂。”妈妈笑着说。

paras.en: “Without anybody left in the house but us, this place could use a bit of fun.
paras.zh: “家里除了我们俩，一个人都没剩下，这地方真该添点乐趣了。

paras.en: Let’s get a little dog for Poppy.”
paras.zh: 咱们给波比找只小狗吧。”

paras.en: It didn’t take long before they walked through the front door carrying a big box.
paras.zh: 没过多久，他们就抱着一个大箱子走进了前门。

paras.en: Poppy welcomed them home as usual but when she saw the box, she stopped.
paras.zh: 波比像往常一样欢迎他们回家，可一看到箱子，它就停住了。

paras.en: She put her nose on it.
paras.zh: 它把鼻子凑到箱子上。

paras.en: Her tail began wagging (摆动) ever so slowly, then faster as she caught the smell.
paras.zh: 它的尾巴开始极慢地摆动，等闻到气味后，摆得越来越快。

paras.en: Dad opened the box and a sweet little dog appeared.
paras.zh: 爸爸打开箱子，一只可爱的小狗出现了。

paras.en: A few weeks later, the boy arrived home from university.
paras.zh: 几个星期后，男孩从大学回到了家。
